title: Bonus Chapter: Spear Hero, Delivered Early, 2023
text: “Fguah!”
Just as I thought I was about to leap into a new loop, I plummeted at incredible speed and slammed straight into the ground.
“Oh my… I was going to set it to random and send you off, but who’d have thought you’d draw this one.”
“W-why is that, I say?”

“Well, you see, Professor Ark went out of his way to make sure you wouldn’t get hurt… Aren’t you lucky? If things had gone as planned, you would’ve been flung into a loop that would’ve been pretty rough on you. Specifically, one involving the thing you fear most—Filo-chan’s—”
“Hyiiiiiii!?”
Just from that alone, I knew exactly which loop it meant. So Ark had set up some kind of mechanism to prevent that from happening!?

“There were others too—loops where you drove him to the absolute brink, loops that were bad news for both you and him—they’ve all had the same treatment and aren’t even constructed anymore, so those branches simply don’t exist. So, we could just redo the draw, but… no… actually.”
The Spirit of the Spear seemed to mull something over, then lit up as if struck by an idea.

“Right. If I use that… hehe, I could do something interesting. There are traces in your world too of someone else having pulled a similar trick, so, yeah. It’s interesting, and the timing’s just right, so let’s try it. A little leeway like this should be fine.”
“Muttering to yourself doesn’t tell me a thing, I say.”

“Well, of course it doesn’t—I’m trying to surprise you, after all. Let’s see… while we’re at it, why don’t I explain why summoning heroes has to be initiated from the human side? Originally, it was optional. I could summon whenever I liked, too.”

Hmm, indeed—if the spirits possessed will of their own, then surely it would be better for the summoned as well if the spirits could call them at will. Strange places… Father suffered for that very reason, did he not, I say.

“But every time the worlds fuse together, that sort of thing becomes harder to do. Things that were originally separate end up stuck together, after all. It’s like the specifications stop matching up. So it becomes more a matter of calling through the holes opened by human-side summonings, whenever the opportunity arises.”
“Is that so, I say.”

So that is why hero summonings exist. Then the very first hero of the sacred weapons must have been someone the spirit could summon and place whenever necessary, I say. Hmm… so even spirits find it troublesome not being able to call freely. Oh? Perhaps now would be a good time to ask something.
“Something’s been nagging at me, I say.”
“What?”
“It’s a question I’d rather ask the Shield Spirit directly, if I could, I say.”
“Ah, but you’ll probably never meet her, so you’d best ask me instead.”
“Then I shall ask, I say. Why does Father have so little attack power, I say?”
I had assumed it was simply the build the Shield Spirit had chosen, but I figured I’d confirm it properly.
“Ah, that? Well, that’s not the Shield Spirit’s fault. In fact, there were heroes chosen by the Shield Spirit in the past who did have attack capability.”
What!? So heroes of the shield other than Father, in ages past, could actually attack!
“It’s simply a matter of his nature. He originally belongs to the realm of dreams and illusions, you see.”
“Infinite, you say? Indeed, Father does possess infinite mercy, I say.”
“Not that kind of ‘infinite’—I mean dreams and illusions, like a mirage. There’s no way it’d be the kind of ‘infinite’ Professor Ark hates.”
Dreams and illusions? Was the Spirit of the Spear even aware she was using such specialized terminology? I hardly understood a word of it, I say.

“Even in a scenario that wasn’t in her prophecy—even if I’d chosen him instead of you—his attack power would still be considerably low. Do you remember? A while back, when the Shield’s sacred weapon was temporarily stolen from him, and the Staff Spirit lent her power? Even then, he was fighting using the original wielder’s attack power borrowed through her. Well, since the opponent was a cheater, some attack power did get added on top, it seems.”

So it appeared that simply holding a weapon inhabited by a spirit applied a negative correction to one’s attack power. Judging from the conversation, she must have been talking about the time Father borrowed a weapon from Trash. Something about teaming up with Tiger Guy to put Takt through absolute hell. As expected of Father, I say. So, in short, it seemed that when Father wields the Shield’s sacred weapon, he simply cannot draw out any attack power from it.
“Could you not dwell within Father’s hand yourself, I say?”

“You know what kind of spirit I am, right? The shield can function passably as auxiliary equipment, sure. But— in that case, it would have to go through you, and in that loop, there’s the matter of connecting your memories and stats and all that. Ah, if we swapped it, you’d end up lost with nowhere to go, and it wouldn’t turn out well besides. I don’t think you’d be able to get through his situation, you know?”

The Spirit of the Spear seemed to have run some calculations and declared it impossible. Guh… I say. That alone told me just how dire Father’s circumstances must have been. Come to think of it, back in those days, I didn’t possess anywhere near the survival skills Father had, I say.
“Anyway, that’s enough talk for now… The world you’re headed to next is, shall we say, something like a bonus stage.”
“A bonus stage, you say?”

“Well, whether it counts as a bonus stage for you, I can’t really say? But it’s true, as you always say—it’s precisely because everyone has repeated their regrets over and over, countless times, that there are places one can only reach this way.”
And with that, my body began to float upward once more, weightless.
“Now then, Motoyasu Kitamura—let’s see what kind of actions you take in the next world.”
The Spirit of the Spear spoke as though testing me, I say.
“Knowing you, I’m sure it’ll be fine. Just go with whatever your heart commands. You’re the type who works hard for someone else’s sake, aren’t you?”
“Just what are you spouting off on your own, I say!”
“Oh, one piece of advice, though. The next hero to be summoned is fixed. Keep that in mind.”
I will absolutely turn you into a cart axle again, I say! And so, once more, I found myself looping.

I came to with a start and looked around, I say. Some sort of highway… no, wait, I recognized this place—the very road where Filo-tan and I had our romantic rendezvous, I say. So I figured I must have leapt into that same loop, but Filo-tan was nowhere to be found. I checked my status to see the registered Filolial-samas, but there wasn’t a single one listed, I say. What’s more, my clothing was the plain civilian clothes from right after I’d first arrived in this other world.

??? Just what in the world was going on, I say? Never mind the location—I couldn’t even begin to imagine the situation, I say. After all, right after a loop, one must always try to deduce the circumstances. And yet I couldn’t picture a single thing.

No Filolial-sama, and Father nowhere nearby either. The most plausible explanation was that this was before I’d raised any Filolial-sama, while I was off doing something to help Father. No, wait—even if this was the loop heading to Siltvelt, it should have been nighttime by then, yet unfortunately it was broad daylight, I say. Even considering leaving Éclair behind to chase after someone, the location made no sense. Frankly speaking, not once in any previous loop had I ever ended up in a situation like this, I say.

I ought to search for some clue to judge by, I say. I checked inside my spear for any dropped items, but there was nothing. Just where on earth had she dropped me, I say? I should have asked before looping. She’d called it a bonus stage—I say she ought to have just told me where, plainly. Given how coy and suggestive her attitude had been, the odds she’d deliberately withheld the answer were sky-high, I say. I will absolutely turn her into a cart axle, I say. Perhaps I’ll skewer that fellow through the backside while I’m at it? No, wait, that would just be a reward for him, I say. In any case, let’s gather information first and judge from there.
“Portal Spear!”
And so, as a first step, I decided to warp over to Melromarc via portal.

Having arrived in Melromarc, I checked out the castle town, I say. Nothing in particular seemed to have changed. Storming straight into the castle to threaten Trash was tempting, but if I caused a scene recklessly, Father might scold me for it, I say. So instead, playing the part of a scout, I cloaked myself and checked inside the castle, I say. Hmm… I couldn’t quite make sense of things.

Oh? I spotted Trash inside the castle. Where might the Crimson Swine be, I say? Striking first and beating him to death might not be a bad idea, I say. Thinking so, I followed after Trash, only to find him heading into what looked like a meeting room to speak with someone, I say.
“A letter has arrived saying that Malty, who’ll be coming home soon during the academy’s long break, wants to eat a dish made with some rare ingredient, so I’m thinking of preparing it.”
The other party was… who, exactly, I say? Someone I felt like I’d seen before yet also hadn’t—someone with a familiar face I could’ve sworn I was meeting for the very first time, I say.
“What say you? Are you telling me even this much is too much to ask!”
Trash was saying something that sounded like he was trying to gauge the other person’s mood, I say.
“You too have a daughter of your own, do you not! Are you telling me even that much is forbidden to me!”
“…Understood. I shall prepare it. I’ll see about asking someone from my territory to go out fishing.”
“Good! I leave it to you. Ah, how I long to see that child’s face again.”
Judging by the response, Trash seemed satisfied, I say. And then, as the other person left the room… oh? It seemed Éclair was waiting just outside the door, I say.
As though awaiting orders, I say.
“This time, I shall go myself. I must make the request even knowing it’s an unreasonable one. You stay here at the castle.”
“Yes, sir!”
And Éclair obediently followed the order, it seemed, I say.
“You’re finally returning to your own territory. Please, rest your wings a while, at least.”
At Éclair’s words, the other person appeared to smile, I say.
“Ah, I can’t stay away too long, but I suppose I’ll stretch my wings a bit.”

Hmm…? For Éclair to be walking about the castle so naturally—did that mean this was after the whole Three Heroes Church incident, I say? No, wait—or perhaps, after Trash had a change of heart, I’d ended up in some peaceful stretch of time before the whole wave business even started, I say. I searched the castle but found no sign of Fiancée. Nothing quite clicked into place, so I decided to head to the village on Father’s territory. If it was after peace had settled, that village should generally be under reconstruction by Father’s doing. If it wasn’t, that would raise the possibility this was a loop heading toward Siltvelt. After all, there was a stretch of time when I hadn’t yet confirmed Big Sister was even alive, I say. And so, I headed for Father’s territory—also known as Big Sister’s village.
“Welcome. Are you a traveler?”

Arriving at Big Sister’s village, I found people who looked like villagers there. Had there been villagers like this before, I say? A scattering of unfamiliar faces caught my eye, I say. But it wasn’t unusual for personnel I didn’t recognize to show up, so I answered smoothly enough, I say?
“Just passing through, I say.”
“I see. It’s a small village, but please, take your time.”

So saying, the villager departed, looking somewhat wary. I strolled through the village at a leisurely pace, taking stock of things as I went. Hmm…? For a place that had supposedly been rebuilt, there were quite a few rather old buildings about, I say. I had no idea just when in the timeline I’d ended up looping to, I say. How long had it even been since the wave occurred?
“Excuse me, I say.”
“Yes? What can I do for you, traveler?”
It nagged at me a little, but I pressed on regardless, I say.
“How long has it been since the wave occurred, I say?”
“Huh? What do you mean by ‘wave’? Do you mean that time the sea got a bit rough recently?”
……? Somehow, the conversation simply wasn’t adding up, I say.
“Then would you happen to know where Father—the Shield Hero—might be, I say?”
“The Shield Hero-sama? Now there’s a legendary figure I’d love to meet. I’m sure he’s watching over us from somewhere.”

Was this reaction one of simple ignorance, I say? It sounded like nothing more than a purely religious, deity-like response. Spirit of the Spear, just where on earth had you dropped me, I say? The distant future, perhaps, I say? No, surely not—surely there weren’t lookalikes of Trash and Éclair running around in the future?
“Hello there!”
“Yes, yes. Hello, Raphtalia-chan.”
And just as that conversation was happening nearby… a young Big Sister came dashing merrily past.
“Bu-bu-buuu!”
“Yahoo!”

There stood Keel and Big Sister’s Friend, I say. Both in their young forms, I say. No, there was nothing particularly strange about them appearing young—but for the villagers not to bat an eye at any mention of the wave, that was strange indeed, I say.
“Bubu! Bubuhi?”
“Ball games!”
“Tag!”
“Swimming in the sea sounds nice too—”
“Buboo!”
“Buu!”
And so, Keel and the others, having settled on what to play, headed off toward the outskirts of the village, I say.
“Hey there. Raphtalia, it’s good you’re full of energy, but don’t wander too far, alright?”
“Ah, Father! Okay!”

And there, waving cheerfully at them, stood an adult man of what looked to be the same species as Big Sister, I say. ……? Big Sister, calling him Father…? However I looked at it, the man had ears, a tail, and facial features that clearly spoke of blood ties with Big Sister. But… I’d heard that Big Sister’s birth parents had died in the wave. Struck by realization, I checked the countdown to the wave’s arrival, I say.

The wave hadn’t happened yet… no, wait, did that mean it was about to happen!? In other words, it seemed that I… had looped to a point before this world had even become aware of the wave at all, I say. In this loop, where even Father hadn’t yet been summoned, just what in the world was I supposed to do, I say!?
